body.x: Conventional LiDAR sensors face three limits: the resolution of the 3D data they capture, a narrow vertical field of view and performance that degrades under external vibration. Those limits matter most on machines that shake, such as tractors, drones and robots.
LCHP Tech is developing a sensor aimed at all three at once.

LCHP Tech Co., Ltd., a Daegu-based startup launched in 2023 as an SK hynix in-house venture (Hi-Garage) and led by CEO Yongdae Park, is exhibiting at KES 2026 with a mock-up of its Hyper-LiDAR, which is under performance evaluation, and a model of the upcoming prototype. The company will also show scan images from the mock-up evaluation that demonstrate a vertical resolution of 500 channels, compared with the 50 channels it says are typical of domestic products.

Hyper-LiDAR combines the high-speed, ultra-precise nano-scanning technology of atomic force microscopes (AFM) with hybrid optical technology designed to widen a narrow field of view and reduce physical degradation. According to the company, it delivers more than 10 times the resolution of existing LiDAR products and a vertical scan more than three times wider without optical loss, and the piezo-stack structure of its nano-scanner keeps scanning stable under heavy vibration. LCHP Tech expects it to serve agriculture, including autonomous tractors, defense and robotics.

The company is in the development phase and aims to launch a Hyper-LiDAR prototype in March 2027. It has filed five domestic patent applications, five PCT international applications and one U.S. patent application. It raised seed funding of KRW 200 million (about USD 140,000) in January 2025 and has been selected for government programs including the Preliminary Startup Package, Pre-TIPS, R&D TIPS and the First Penguin program. It showed an early prototype at the SK hynix in-house exhibition in September 2025 and at the Future Innovation tech eXpo (FIX 2025) in October.

LCHP Tech is seeking a partnership with John Deere to develop autonomous tractors. In January 2026, it signed memorandums of understanding with U.S. game software company BRAVE TURTLES on business cooperation and with U.S. investment firm JC-VALLY on strategic investment. Its 2027 roadmap centers on proof-of-concept projects and new partners, and from 2028 it plans to set up local subsidiaries step by step. The company says overseas entry requires laser and optical safety certification (IEC 60825-1, FDA CDRH), electromagnetic compatibility certification (FCC, CE) and automotive electronics testing (ISO 16750), and it would like pre-evaluation support during the design stage.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
